summary: Fined for publishing inaccurate FY22–HY24 financial statements. Management accounting judgements were inappropriately influenced by a desire to maintain previously stated targets.

Banned for acting as regulatory front: sold firm to a disqualified director and concealed beneficial ownership to allow high-risk mini-bond marketing through the FCA authorisation. Investors lost ~£4M.
Fined for insider dealing in Chariot Oil & Gas and Eco Atlantic shares Oct 2018–Jan 2022. Case triggered by STOR filings from broker. Includes £128,765 profit disgorgement.
Combined FinCEN ($500M) + OCC ($450M) + OFAC ($260M) enforcement for systemic AML failures 2019–2024. Inadequate beneficial ownership screening and correspondent banking controls.
Fed and OCC joint fine for AML programme deficiencies: failed CDD for Platinum card clients, inadequate SAR monitoring for prepaid cards, gaps in OFAC screening.

FSCA record fine for using AI deepfake videos (Elon Musk / Johann Rupert) to channel investors into an unlawful scheme; R1bn in client funds misappropriated. Licence revoked; directors debarred 30 years.
MAS revoked Major Payment Institution licence for persistent AML failures — no CDD on cash transactions above S$5,000 for 3 years; no STR filings; inadequate recordkeeping.
BaFin fined Wirecard successor for failing to maintain adequate AML controls and complete client fund records across approximately 2.1 million historical accounts post-insolvency.
ASIC infringement notices for AFSL/ACL breaches including 5 fintech operators with embedded lending products. Highest single notice A$395K for BNPL suitability failure.
SEC charged fintech referral platform for undisclosed conflicts of interest — received compensation from recommended advisers without adequate retail investor disclosure.
BCB enforcement: all banks prohibited from transacting with unlicensed VASPs from 30 Oct 2026. Over 40 crypto startups had not filed for authorisation at the deadline.
FSCA barred from accepting new client funds pending active investigation into suspected unlawful conduct. FSCA investigation opened 5 October 2026.
